title: ZIA locations, sublocations and location groups

prose.text: "Which policy applies to this traffic's location?" needs more than the location's name. A location identifies a network the service recognizes by its settings, it can be split into sublocations that match by IP, and rules reach both directly and through groups. Work down this list; the parent [[zia.firewall]] and rule subjects are linked at the end.

steps.label: What is the location, and what does the service do with it?
steps.text: Known locations are processed by their settings; anything else is remote-user traffic: [[zia.locations.model]].

steps.label: Is the traffic in a sublocation?
steps.text: Matching is by the IP inside the tunnel or the XFF address, sublocations cannot overlap, and unmatched traffic falls to `other`: [[zia.locations.sublocations]], [[zia.locations.ip-scoping]].

steps.label: Which settings does the sublocation have of its own?
steps.text: Some are parent-only in the API, and the console and API disagree on firewall: [[zia.locations.inheritance]]. Bandwidth has its own modes: [[zia.locations.bandwidth]].

steps.label: Which groups is it in?
steps.text: Location type, defaults and exclusion flags decide this at creation, and dynamic groups change it later: [[zia.locations.groups]], [[zia.locations.group-assignment]].

steps.label: Which rules reach it?
steps.text: Rules take locations and groups: [[zia.locations.rule-scoping]]. Per-module effects are in [[zia.url-filtering]], [[zia.ssl-inspection]], [[zia.cloud-app-control]], [[zia.firewall]] and [[zia.dlp]].

prose.text: Workload sublocations on AWS have scopes and different overlap rules: [[zia.locations.workload-scopes]]. Country and time zone values, including the `THE_` prefix: [[zia.locations.country-timezone]]. Writing locations through the API, Terraform or Ansible, including lookups that miss sublocations: [[zia.locations.automation]], [[zia.sdk-go.service-defects]], [[zia.terraform.data-source-fidelity]].
